modules.title: AF ablation: reading the CTSN trial
modules.summary: Rhythm benefit, pacemaker trade-off and the importance of endpoint units.

sections.heading: Study question
sections.text: Gillinov and colleagues randomised 260 patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF requiring mitral-valve surgery to concomitant ablation or no ablation. All patients underwent left atrial appendage closure. This is a specific surgical population, not all patients with AF. [aftrial]

sections.heading: What was measured
sections.text: Freedom from AF at both six and twelve months was assessed using three-day Holter monitoring: 63.2% with ablation versus 29.4% without. Do not describe this as continuous freedom from AF over an entire year. [aftrial]

sections.heading: Benefit and harm
sections.text: Permanent pacemaker implantation rates were 21.5 versus 8.1 per 100 patient-years. These are incidence rates, not percentages. One-year mortality did not differ significantly; the hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI 0.32–1.84). [aftrial]

sections.heading: Viva interpretation
sections.text: Explain the rhythm benefit and increased pacemaker rate together. A non-significant mortality result does not demonstrate equivalence or prove no long-term benefit. The paper does not establish that successful ablation permits anticoagulation withdrawal. [aftrial]

objectives: Interpret trial population and endpoint
Report event rates with correct units
Distinguish rhythm control from survival evidence

modules.title: CALGB 140503: what was randomised?
modules.summary: Sublobar versus lobar resection in selected peripheral node-negative disease.

sections.heading: Population and design
sections.text: 697 patients were randomised to sublobar resection or lobectomy. The conclusion applies to peripheral NSCLC no larger than 2 cm with pathologically confirmed negative hilar and mediastinal nodes. [calgb]

sections.heading: Primary result
sections.text: At a median follow-up of seven years, the hazard ratio for recurrence or death was 1.01, with a 90% confidence interval of 0.83–1.24. Sublobar resection met the trial’s noninferiority criterion for disease-free survival. [calgb]

sections.heading: Absolute outcomes
sections.text: Five-year disease-free survival was 63.6% after sublobar resection and 64.1% after lobar resection. Overall survival was similar: HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.72–1.26. [calgb]

sections.heading: Limits of application
sections.text: This was not a randomised wedge-versus-segmentectomy comparison. Do not generalise the trial to larger, central or node-positive tumours or substitute radiological staging alone for its pathological nodal requirements. [calgb]

objectives: Define the eligible population
Explain noninferiority
Avoid a wedge-versus-segmentectomy inference

modules.title: JCOG0802: survival and local relapse
modules.summary: Keep survival, relapse and analysis dates separate.

sections.heading: Study population
sections.text: The original JCOG0802/WJOG4607L report compared segmentectomy with lobectomy for peripheral NSCLC no larger than 2 cm with a consolidation-to-tumour ratio greater than 0.5. This is not the same question as an unrestricted sublobar comparison. [jcog]

sections.heading: Original overall-survival analysis
sections.text: Five-year overall survival was 94.3% with segmentectomy and 91.1% with lobectomy; HR 0.663, 95% CI 0.474–0.927. These figures belong to the original 2022 report. [jcog]

sections.heading: Local control matters
sections.text: Local relapse occurred in 10.5% versus 5.4%, respectively. Five-year relapse-free survival was 88.0% versus 87.9%. An overall-survival result does not mean better local control. [jcog]

sections.heading: Publication versions
sections.text: Do not merge later conference follow-up with the original result. A ten-year update is not numerically included here because its original dataset has not been independently checked for this build. [jcog]

objectives: Distinguish survival from local control
Keep analysis versions separate

modules.title: Comparing the two sublobar trials
modules.summary: Related trials, different randomised comparisons.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.text: JCOG0802 randomised segmentectomy versus lobectomy; CALGB 140503 randomised sublobar resection (wedge or segmentectomy) versus lobectomy. Their populations, comparisons and primary endpoints must be described separately. [jcog] [calgb]

sections.heading: Exam application
sections.text: In a viva, establish eligibility, nodal assessment and achievable resection before using a trial to support a proposal. Neither trial randomised every small nodule to every resection option. [jcog] [calgb]

objectives: Compare randomised interventions
Recognise external-validity limits

modules.title: The 2026 curriculum: what changed
modules.summary: New index procedures and emerging practice in the official change document.

sections.heading: Index procedures
sections.text: The update adds isolated uncomplicated mitral valve replacement and resection of a mediastinal lesion; it clarifies isolated uncomplicated AVR and decortication and/or washout of empyema. Robotic approaches are included within anatomical lung resection. [changes]

sections.heading: New and expanded knowledge
sections.text: Changes include minimal-access approaches, non-A non-B aortic dissection, frozen elephant trunk and head-and-neck debranching techniques, and standalone AF surgery. [changes]

sections.heading: Professional themes
sections.text: Genomics, clinical informatics and sustainability are made explicit. The change document acknowledges unequal training opportunities and does not require all trainees to fully evidence these emerging areas at this stage. [changes]

sections.heading: Scope of this app
sections.text: Curriculum knowledge, examination preparation and operative workplace competence are different. This beta provides learning support, not certification or an official syllabus completion assessment. [iscp]

objectives: Identify revised index procedures
Separate knowledge from operative competence

modules.summary: An index procedure is not a claim of exam weighting.

sections.heading: Updated operative scope
sections.text: The August 2026 change document updates cardiac and thoracic index procedures and clarifies assessment-level wording. It distinguishes expected operative familiarity and levels of supervision. [changes]

sections.heading: How to revise
sections.text: Use each operation as a learning scaffold: indication, anatomy, preparation, sequence, hazards, rescue, postoperative assessment and consent. This is an original study structure, not an official marking scheme.

sections.heading: What progress means
sections.text: A self-rated confidence score in this app is not a PBA and does not demonstrate independent operative competence. Use the formal curriculum and workplace assessment process. [iscp]

modules.title: Evidence appraisal: a surgical viva framework
modules.summary: Practise describing what a paper establishes—and what it does not.

sections.heading: Start with the actual question
sections.text: State population, intervention, comparator and measured outcome. For CALGB 140503, that means a selected peripheral node-negative population and disease-free survival, not a randomised wedge-versus-segmentectomy question. [calgb]

sections.heading: Report uncertainty
sections.text: Report the confidence interval, its level and the analysis time point. CALGB reported a 90% CI for its primary DFS comparison; the original JCOG overall-survival result reported a 95% CI. Do not silently standardise them. [calgb] [jcog]

sections.heading: Separate endpoints
sections.text: The CTSN AF trial illustrates why improved rhythm control and pacemaker risk belong in the same discussion; its mortality analysis is not a substitute for its rhythm endpoint. [aftrial]

sections.heading: Editorial standard
sections.text: For any new paper, record original versus secondary analysis, abstract versus full-text access, population limits, funding/conflicts, and whether a correction or retraction has been checked. This is the app’s proposed review policy, not a society recommendation.

objectives: Explain external validity
Report confidence intervals accurately
Distinguish clinical endpoints

questions.stem: In the CTSN mitral-surgery trial, how should the reported pacemaker values 21.5 versus 8.1 be expressed?
options: Percentages at 30 days
Implantations per 100 patient-years
Risk ratios
Median time to implantation in days
questions.explanation: They are incidence rates per 100 patient-years, not percentages. Preserve the original unit and reporting interval.

questions.stem: Which outcome defined the CTSN trial’s primary rhythm endpoint?
options: A single normal discharge ECG
No AF on a six-month ECG alone
Freedom from AF at both six and twelve months on three-day Holter assessment
Continuous implantable-loop monitoring without any AF for one year
questions.explanation: The primary endpoint used three-day Holter recordings at both assessments; this is not continuous year-long monitoring.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is supported by CALGB 140503?
options: Wedge resection was randomised against segmentectomy and proved superior
Sublobar resection was noninferior for DFS in the trial’s selected peripheral, pathologically node-negative population
All central tumours should undergo wedge resection
Imaging alone replaced pathological nodal assessment
questions.explanation: The randomised comparison was sublobar versus lobar resection, in a carefully defined population. Wedge versus segmentectomy was not the randomised comparison.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly describes the original JCOG0802 segmentectomy result compared with lobectomy?
options: Lower overall survival and lower local relapse
Higher five-year overall survival and higher local relapse
Identical overall survival and no local relapse
A randomised wedge-versus-segmentectomy benefit
questions.explanation: The original report found five-year OS 94.3% versus 91.1%, with local relapse 10.5% versus 5.4%. The endpoints must not be conflated.

questions.stem: What confidence level accompanied CALGB 140503’s primary DFS hazard ratio of 1.01?
questions.explanation: The primary result used a 90% CI of 0.83–1.24. Do not silently relabel it 95%.

questions.stem: Which item was added as a cardiac index procedure in the August 2026 changes?
options: All complex mitral repairs
Heart transplantation
Isolated uncomplicated mitral valve replacement
Every hybrid arch procedure
questions.explanation: The official change document adds isolated uncomplicated MVR. An index procedure is not a question-frequency prediction.

questions.stem: Why should a later conference update not overwrite the original trial result without qualification?
options: Conference results are always false
Analysis date, follow-up, population and publication status must be preserved
Older publications must always take precedence
Only statistically significant results can be stored
questions.explanation: Preserve publication versions. Later findings may be important, but must be individually checked and labelled; do not combine incompatible analyses.

questions.stem: What does marking a chapter as read demonstrate in this app?
options: Independent operative competence
An official PBA result
An activity record only
Guaranteed FRCS readiness
questions.explanation: Reading and self-rating are learning records, not formal operative or examination assessments.

vivas.title: Does the AF trial change your operation?
vivas.stem: A patient with long-standing persistent AF requires mitral-valve surgery. You are asked what the CTSN trial contributes to counselling.
prompts: Define the trial population and intervention.
State the rhythm endpoint and results.
Explain the pacemaker trade-off using correct units.
What did the study not establish?
points: 260 patients undergoing mitral surgery; ablation versus no ablation; all had appendage closure.
Freedom from AF at both 6 and 12 months: 63.2% versus 29.4%.
Do not claim established long-term survival benefit or permission to withdraw anticoagulation.

vivas.title: Can this small lung cancer have a lesser resection?
vivas.stem: An examiner asks whether CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802 answer exactly the same question.
points: CALGB: sublobar versus lobar; JCOG: segmentectomy versus lobectomy.
Small peripheral lesions; state each trial’s particular eligibility and nodal requirements.
CALGB DFS noninferiority; original JCOG OS improvement with more local relapse.
Neither is a randomised demonstration that wedge and segmentectomy are interchangeable in all patients.

vivas.title: The curriculum has changed—what matters?
vivas.stem: A junior resident asks what the August 2026 update means for their learning plan.
prompts: Distinguish educational progress from formal competence.
points: Isolated uncomplicated MVR added; isolated uncomplicated AVR clarified.
Mediastinal lesion resection added; empyema and robotic approach wording updated.
Anatomy/physiology, function tests, injury/repair and aerodigestive fistula assessment and management.
Use formal curriculum and workplace assessments; app self-ratings are not certification.
